quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects the wearer from:

options.text: Insects.
Headlight glare.
Noise.
Sunshine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Insects.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and pebbles. It also protects your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: How is the accelerator controlled?

options.text: With the right hand
With the left hand
With the right foot
With the left foot

questions.correctAnswerText: With the right hand
questions.explanation: The accelerator is located by the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: Which of the following is not important when looking for a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no obvious defects, such as cracks or loose padding.
The helmet looks cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks cool.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. DOT standards, fit snugly around your entire head, and have no visible damage like cracks or loose padding. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: Slippery surfaces can make it difficult to control a motorcycle. Which of the following would be considered a slippery surface?

options.text: Wet pavement
A driveway
Dry pavement
A parking lot

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are slippery surfaces. Ride with extra caution on these surfaces.

questions.question: Most crashes occur in broad daylight. To be more visible, you should:

options.text: Wear brightly-colored clothing.
Wear dark clothing.
Ride without your headlight.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear brightly-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright colors when riding, even during the day, to make yourself more visible.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: Before every ride.
About once every 10 rides.
Once a month.
Once a season.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small problem can be much more dangerous on a motorcycle than on a car. Check your motorcycle before every ride.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a dangerously slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: When you can't avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle straight and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you:

options.text: When conditions will make stopping more difficult than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver in front of you from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions will make stopping more difficult than usual.
questions.explanation: You need extra space when your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Leave a larger following distance when pavement is slippery, visibility is poor, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Which of the following should you inspect during a pre-ride check?

options.text: The general wear and tread of your tires
The amount of cushion your seat has
The shine of your paint
The wind direction

questions.correctAnswerText: The general wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If you can, change lanes and let a tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause the driver to tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When a motorcycle rider downshifts smoothly:

options.text: It serves no useful purpose.
It allows the rider to use engine braking.
It is against the law.
It should not be done around other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows the rider to use engine braking.
questions.explanation: Downshifting smoothly can help slow the motorcycle using engine braking. If you use engine braking, use your brake lights separately to warn other drivers that you are slowing down.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, a motorcycle rider should watch out for:

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking spot.
Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
Oncoming traffic.
Loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked vehicles. A car may pull away from the curb or exit a parking space suddenly.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
Easier to see than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually harder to see than a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers notice you are braking.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider should always scan the road ahead for:

options.text: Road conditions.
Traffic conditions.
Escape routes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Scan ahead to watch for changing traffic, hazardous road conditions, and escape routes. Be ready to react quickly to any change.

questions.question: The most important thing you can do to survive a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a quality helmet that is fastened securely.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a quality helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a quality helmet that is securely fastened is the single best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: ____ removes alcohol from your body.

options.text: Time
Coffee
Exercise
Fresh air

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time reduces the amount of alcohol in your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change how much alcohol is in your system.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, remember that motorcycles:

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots too small to cause problems.
Have blind spots that require you to check your head.
Have only one blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that require you to check your head.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend in with traffic and stay unnoticed.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your turn signals, brake lights, and proper lane position to show your intentions. Keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: When getting ready to pass another vehicle, ride in the left part of your lane because it:

options.text: Improves your view of the road ahead.
Blocks your view of the road ahead.
Makes it hard to see around the vehicle.
Lets the other driver go faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Improves your view of the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see further ahead and makes other drivers more likely to notice you in the passing lane.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Skip multiple gears at once.
Shift down one gear at a time.
Always go down to neutral first.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: Downshift one gear at a time. Let the clutch out slowly through the friction zone between each downshift.

questions.question: When you drink alcohol faster:

options.text: More alcohol builds up in your body.
Your body removes alcohol faster.
The effects of alcohol are less severe.
You are less likely to be pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: More alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink faster, more alcohol builds up in your body. It is never safe to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When riding on a bridge grating, you should:

options.text: Always stay on the far right side of your lane.
Always stay on the far left side of your lane.
Slowly zigzag across the grating.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is usually not dangerous. Stay calm and ride straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging to avoid the weave is dangerous because it forces you out of your lane.

questions.question: Common drugs like cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect your ability to ride safely.
Usually do not affect your ability to ride safely.
Do not affect your riding ability.
Are always safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medications, can affect your riding ability. Learn about the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than usual.
Ride more slowly than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more space to stop. Ride slower, start braking sooner, give yourself more space, and wait for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants:

options.text: Should completely cover your arms and legs.
Should be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Should only partially cover your arms and legs.
Should be made of wool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should completely cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should completely cover your arms and legs. They should fit snug but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in an accident.
